# 5. Hits and blocks are identified by byte spans, and blocks form a tree

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-11-11

## Context

A block is a line range plus a copy of its text (`CodeBlock { line_start, line_end, code, .. }`, `types.rs`) and a hit is a whole line (`LineHit { line_number, text }`). Both analyzers hold the exact span when they build a block (`push_block` in `analysis/ts/parse.rs`, `record` in `analysis/rust/parse.rs`) and drop it after cutting lines and `code`. The tree is dropped too: `parent` is a `ParentContext { kind, name }`, not a link to a block.

Later stages re-derive structure from lines or text. Non-test code mentions `line_start`, `line_end`, `matched_lines`, `line_number` or `code` on 87 lines in 11 files. The guessing stages:

- `owned_hits` (`pipeline/mod.rs`) picks a hit's owner by line range, own-text matching, and `outer.code.contains(inner.code)` for equal ranges.
- `snippet` and `signature_shows` (`output/agent.rs`) decide by text whether the signature already shows the first line.
- `encloses_member` and `overlaps_significantly` (`dedup.rs`) compare line ranges, so two disjoint blocks on one line overlap fully.
- `name_match_boost` (`rank/boost.rs`) cuts a signature string at `(`, `<`, `{`, `=`, `:` to recover a name.

The same gap produced 7 fix or test commits in 3 PRs (#66: 3, #68: 1, #77: 3). Ownership was rewritten three times (earliest of equal size, innermost by range, own text on the line) for `} b() {`, `}, // note` and `const a = 1; const needle = 2;`. A test function and its module with the same range were credited twice. A first-line snippet repeated or hid the signature. `pub(crate) fn` was cut to `pub`. `pipeline/proptests.rs` re-implements the old rule as its reference, so it pins the rule, not a contract.

## Decision

We recommend identifying hits and blocks by byte spans and linking blocks into a forest.

- A hit carries its line and the offsets at which its matches start, as ranges of consecutive offsets (a pattern that matches every byte of a line is one range). Where a match ends is not needed: ownership reads the first byte.
- A block carries a byte span and its parent's index in the file's block list, built once by the analyzer.
- The AST supplies `name` and `kind` as typed fields.
- Ownership is per match, in this order. Each match goes to the innermost block whose span contains its first byte (equal spans resolve by parent depth, not text). A match no block contains, which sits where a block's span ends, goes to the innermost block that ends there; the end is inclusive only when no block contains the offset, so a zero-width `$` after a declaration belongs to it. A hit that no match credited goes to the innermost blocks at each byte of its line. A hit goes once to every block credited. (Decided per match, not per hit: `const a = 1; const needle = 2;` searched for `const` has a match in each block, and the line-based rule credited both.)
- The invariant: every matched line with a byte in at least one block credits at least one block, so a block is never dropped for lack of a hit while a match touches it. A line no block touches is a match outside every declaration and has no block to return.
- The sink finds the starts of each pattern on its own and merges them. The searcher's alternation matches left to right without overlap, so one pattern's match (`class.*`) could hide another's (`m`).
- Snippets are cut from spans and dedup compares spans.

## Consequences

Deleted: own-text matching and the equal-range rule in `owned_hits`, `signature_shows`, the head-cutting in `name_match_boost` with its `unrestricted` special case, and the proptest's reference reimplementation.

Costs:

- `LineHit` grows a list of match start offsets. The searcher does not give them: `SinkMatch` in `grep-searcher` 0.1.17 (`sink.rs:379-423`) exposes only `bytes()`, `absolute_byte_offset()` and `line_number()` for the whole line. In-line offsets need `Matcher::find_iter` (`grep-matcher` 0.1.9, `lib.rs:629`) over each matching line. `LineCollector::text_matches` (`text_search.rs`) already makes that second pass for CRLF lines.
- Offsets must mean the same bytes on both sides. The searcher sees raw file bytes and the analyzer sees the lossy-decoded `String`, which differ after any invalid UTF-8.
- Each block gains a span (16 bytes) and a parent index (4 to 8 bytes). `code` stays, so nested blocks keep duplicating text.
- Dedup compares bytes instead of lines, the one stage whose output can change beyond the old bugs.

## Alternatives considered

Keep line ranges and patch each case, as we did. It costs a commit per new line shape, and each patch adds a rule the next must respect.

## Order of work

Three PRs. After each, `scripts/rg-compare.py` must not drop: identifier 58/59, questions 17/18, members 15/16, Rust fd 22/24, held-out 23/24 and 12/12. Output is byte-identical except the cases the old rules got wrong, which each PR lists.

1. Analyzers emit spans, parent indices, `name` and `kind`. Nothing reads them yet. Tests assert spans slice to `code`.
2. The sink reports match ranges and `owned_hits` becomes innermost-containing. Test-first: the three line shapes above and the same-range test function and module.
3. `snippet`, `name_match_boost` and `dedup_blocks` read spans and typed fields.

## Not measured

Memory and time of the second regex pass and the spans on a large repo. How many harness queries change under byte-based dedup. Whether mapping lossy offsets beats searching decoded text. How many of the 87 sites would change.

## 34. A held-out set and a Rust gate join the harness (2026-11-10)

- **Decision.** Three repositories that no ranking change was tuned on (fastify, trpc, date-fns) carry 24 multi-word and 12 member questions, written and checked with `rg` before monokl first ran on them. They score on their own lines (`held-out questions`, `held-out members`) and the Rust rows on the pinned fd checkout pool into one `--min-rust-recall` rate. The three gates default to 0.9.
- **Why.** The declared-name bonus (§32) was tuned and scored on the same 18 questions, so 17 of 18 was optimistic. The held-out set scored 23 of 24 and 12 of 12 on first run, close to the tuned 17 of 18 and 15 of 16, which is evidence the bonus and member rows generalize. Rust scored 22 of 24 (11 of 13 identifiers, 11 of 11 questions, 11 of 11 members) once the analyzer landed.
- **Rule.** Ranking changes may be tuned on the tuned sets and must be reported on the held-out set. A held-out miss is never fixed by editing the question.
- **Open.** The sets are small, so one miss moves a rate by 4 points; read them as a regression guard, not an estimate. The one held-out miss is trpc `create websocket client` (answer file at rank 7).

## 35. Reads, hit lines and run time have stated bounds (2026-11-11)

Follows [ADR 0004](../adr/0004-search-stays-stateless-and-every-stage-has-a-stated-bound.md) rules 2 to 4 (PR 88).

- **Decision.** Text search reads at most 4 MiB of a file (`MAX_FILE_BYTES`), checked on the open handle. A larger file is skipped unread and reported as one grouped line. A hit line is kept to 4096 bytes (`MAX_LINE_BYTES`) and the cut lines are counted in a warning. `--timeout SECONDS` defaults to 30, accepts fractions, and 0 disables it. It is checked between files in text search and between batches in analysis. Each stage always finishes its first batch, so a tiny timeout still returns something. An expired run prints `partial result: ... expired after searching|analyzing N of M files` and exits 0. `tests/scaling.rs` takes the fastest of 5 runs at 2,500 and 10,000 inputs for rank and dedup, text search and a whole search, and asserts the time ratio stays under 10 (a quadratic step gives 16). It never asserts absolute times.
- **Why.** The limit equals the 4 MiB parse cap, so a larger file could only come back as too large to parse after being read whole. On the PR's measurements a directory of forty 5 MB files peaked at 479 MB and one 300 MB line at 752 MB; both are now about 5 MB.
- **Partial results.** They are the only output that differs between runs, because which files are reached depends on speed. A `-term` exclusion applies only to the files reached. Without a timeout, output is deterministic.
- **Cost of the line cap.** A term that matches only past byte 4096 of a line is not seen by required-term and keyword checks, and since §42 the hit has no match start, though its line still goes to the blocks on it. The warning says so.

## 36. Parse on a fixed stack behind a nesting scan (2026-11-11)

Replaces §23's per-byte stack and its size caps (PR 83).

- **Decision.** Every parse runs on one 256 MiB stack (`PARSE_STACK_BYTES`). A linear scan (`analysis/nesting.rs`) estimates the recursion a file can cause and rejects it before any parser sees it. The cap is 16,384 levels for TypeScript and 256 for Rust. A rejected file is degraded as too deep and named in the diagnostic with its depth and cap. The post-parse tree-depth check and its leaked trees are gone, because no accepted tree is deeper than the drop thread holds. The size cap is 4 MiB (35).
- **Why.** §23's stack grew with the input, so whether a file was analyzed depended on its length and the host's memory. A fixed stack makes cost and outcome a function of the file alone. §23 deleted the scan because it rejected valid files; the scan now errs only upward and is tested against the real parsers.
- **A false rejection, found and fixed.** The first cap (4,096 levels on a 64 MiB stack) rejected a component with 3,000 sibling JSX elements: its true depth is about 3, but closers do not lower the estimate, so it cost about 45,000 units. The cap and the stack grew by 4x together to keep the margin (the worst nesting at the cap needed 96 MiB and overflowed 64 MiB, so 256 MiB is at least 2.6x). End-to-end tests cover 3,000 JSX siblings, a 12,000-term concatenation and a 20,000-row array.
- **Three soundness bugs found by review, fixed.** `for await (` lost its loop head to `await`. A `;` in JSX text reset what the open elements had charged. Each ambiguous `/` rescanned its whole line. Each has a test that parses the input in a child process on a small stack to show the hazard is real.
- **A differential fuzzer.** `soundness_tests.rs` generates nesting-heavy token soups, scans them under a cap scaled to an 8 MiB stack, and parses every accepted input in a child process. An abort is a counterexample. It found more under-estimates, all fixed with regression tests: a template `}` inside a possible regex flipped backtick parity; Rust 2024 `#"` is a prefix, not a string; unterminated strings, templates, comments and raw strings hid the rest of the source; and the Rust cap let trees deeper than the drop thread holds (now 256 levels). On the final code the PR run found no counterexample.
- **Evidence, not proof.** The fuzzer samples inputs; it does not prove the scan never under-estimates. `MONOKL_FUZZ_SECONDS` sets the run length. The estimate stays a deliberate over-estimate wherever the scan cannot tell syntax apart.
- **Threads are reused within a search.** A thread per parse cost 3.5 s of CPU against 35 ms of parsing over 20,000 files on 18 cores, mostly mapping and unmapping 256 MiB stacks. A search now starts its analysis threads once with that stack (`with_parse_threads`), no more than it has files, and none when nothing matched; a parse on one of them runs in place. A parse anywhere else still gets its own thread. The stack, the nesting scan and the 4 MiB cap are unchanged.
- **Open.** A valid file over the cap loses its results and the user sees it by name.

## 37. Deletions of code nothing reads (2026-11-11)

PRs 84 to 87. Each removed code whose only reader was a test or nothing.

- **Decision.** The query module is crate-private, and tests that scanned source text, probed for absent derives or re-checked exhaustiveness are deleted (PR 84). `coverage_boost` is gone (PR 85): every printed block holds a matching line, so it was a constant 1.0, and `finalScore` is 1.0 lower with the order unchanged. The score breakdown fields and `SearchResponse` totals that only tests read are gone, and `SymbolKind` derives `Ord` instead of mirroring it by hand. `--max-bytes`, `Budget.max_bytes`, the `miette` feature and dependency, and `ToonProjection<N>` are gone (PR 86); `render_search` and `search_row_texts` replace the projection, and `apply_budget` takes the printed row texts. Unread analyzer output is gone (PR 87): symbols, dependencies, exports, JSX, `LangData`, the `Digest` and its `blake3` dependency, `AnalysisProfile`, `AnalyzerCapabilities`, `language_for`, `matched_keywords`, `RankedBlock.parent_context` and `ParentContext.line`. `LanguageAnalyzer` is now `languages`, `supports` and `analyze(path, text)`.
- **Why.** Search reads only `blocks`, `test_blocks`, `had_parse_errors` and `degradation`. `--max-tokens` is `ceil(bytes / 3)`, so the 2 MiB byte cap bound only above about 700,000 tokens. CLI errors render through michi's `DomainError`, so the `miette` derives had no use. Unique crates in the workspace tree went from 252 to 232. PR 87 removed 2,440 lines and added 308, and the release binary went from 3,762,592 to 3,696,240 bytes. Output was byte-identical on 101 queries (87) and on 93 comparisons (86; only `search --help` differs).
- **Consequences.** `--max-bytes` is now a usage error (exit 2). A command that needs a removed field restores it with its analyzer output and a reader. [ADR 0002](../adr/0002-digest-lives-in-monokl-until-wisp-contracts.md) stands for whoever re-adds `Digest`. `LanguageId` keeps `TypeScript` and `Rust`.
- **Open.** The `Language`/`LanguageId` unification. The architecture docs still describe `miette` and `max_bytes`.

## 38. Process lessons (2026-11-11)

- **Decision.** Compile and test the combined state before merging a PR that other PRs touch, and run the soundness tests under plain `cargo test` as well as `nextest`.
- **Why.** Two merges broke `main` because each PR passed alone. The object-member score tests (PR 70) were written before the name bonus (§32) and failed once both were in. The scaling test (PR 88) constructed a field that a deletion (PR 85) removed; PR 90 fixed it. CI on a branch checks that branch against the `main` it started from, not against what merges beside it.
- **A real race hid behind one runner.** The soundness tests passed under `nextest` (one process per test) but shared one batch file under `cargo test`, where concurrent child launches overwrote each other's file and removed each other's directory. Each batch now has its own directory (PR 89).

## 39. A block carries the name its analyzer read from the syntax tree (2026-11-12)

- **Decision.** `CodeBlock` gains `name: Option<String>`, filled by both analyzers for every block that declares an identifier, and `name_match_boost` tokenizes it. §32's text-derived name (the signature or first non-comment line, cut at `(`, `<`, `{`, `=` or `:`, with a `pub(crate)` special case for Rust) is deleted. This is the `name` slice of [ADR 0005](../adr/0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md); spans and parent indices stay open.
- **What the name is.** A function, class, interface, type alias, enum, namespace, method, property or constant has its identifier. An `impl` has its target, or `Trait for Target`, the same string its members use as `parent.name`. A member key that is a string literal or a private identifier has its text; a computed key has none. A declaration of several variables takes the first plain identifier. A re-export, an anonymous default export, a destructuring declaration, a macro call and an `extern` block have `None` and get no name boost.
- **Why.** The head of a line is not a name: it held modifiers (`get`, `static`, `default`) and the type of a variable as words, and needed a `pub(crate)` rule because `(` ends the head. The tree has the name.
- **Output.** No column is added. Scores differ only where the old head held a word the name does not (a modifier, or the type of a variable) and for `export default Button;`, which now has no name because it declares none. The harness is unchanged: identifier 58/59, questions 17/18, members 15/16, Rust fd 22/24, held-out 23/24 and 12/12.
- **Not done.** A typed `ParsedTerm` for ranking. `rank_blocks` and `name_match_boost` take BM25 tokens, which are lowercased fragments of the user's words and not query terms, and `ParsedTerm` already types the one place a query term is read (`QueryPlan`). A wrapper around `&str` tokens would add a type with no new check.

## 40. Blocks carry a byte span and a parent index (2026-11-14)

- **Decision.** `CodeBlock` gains `span: Range<usize>` and `parent_index: Option<usize>`, set by both analyzers from the span and the enclosing block they already hold when they build a block. Nothing reads them. This is step 1 of [ADR 0005](../adr/0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md); `name` landed in §39 and `kind` was already typed (`node_kind`), so steps 2 (match ranges in the sink, innermost-containing `owned_hits`) and 3 (snippets, name boost and dedup from spans) remain.
- **Index space.** `parent_index` counts `FileAnalysis::blocks` followed by `FileAnalysis::test_blocks`. The Rust analyzer splits test code into its own list, and a `#[test]` method of a non-test `impl` has its parent in the other list, so one list per kind cannot hold the link. The analyzer records blocks in one list and renumbers when it splits.
- **Offsets are the analyzer's.** `span` counts bytes of the lossy-decoded source the analyzer received, not of the file. Mapping the searcher's raw offsets onto it is step 2's work, as ADR 0005 states.
- **Output.** None. No reader, no wire change, harness unchanged.

## 41. The held-out set widens to Rust and two more TypeScript and JavaScript styles (2026-11-14)

- **Decision.** Four repositories join the held-out rows, none sampled for identifiers and none tuned on: tokio v1.54.1 (macro-heavy), axum v0.8.9 (trait and impl heavy), react-hook-form v7.92.0 (hooks library) and commander v15.1.0 (class-based JavaScript CLI). Questions were written from READMEs and source with `rg` before monokl ran on them. A repository marked `report-only` in `rg-compare.repos` is scored and printed but never gates. Gated held-out Rust rows pool on a `held-out rust` line (`--min-heldout-rust-recall`, 0.9).
- **First scores.** tokio 16 of 16, axum 18 of 20, commander 19 of 19 (now gated), react-hook-form 12 of 14 (report-only). The older held-out lines are unchanged in rows, now pooled with commander.
- **Misses, left as written.** axum `listener extension` (ListenerExt, answer file at rank 9; `extension.rs` and extractor files outrank it on the word `extension`), axum `extractor from request parts` (FromRequestParts, rank 4; `axum-macros/src/lib.rs` and `with_rejection.rs` outrank the trait file), react-hook-form `watch form values subscribe` (useWatch, rank 4; `types/form.ts`, `useFormContext.tsx` and an `app/` page outrank it) and `create form control` (createFormControl, rank 12; `useFormControlContext.ts`, `useForm.ts` and `examples/` files outrank it).

## 42. A match is credited to the block it starts in (2026-11-14)

Step 2 of [ADR 0005](../adr/0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md). Replaces the line-text rule of §31.

- **Decision.** `LineHit` gains `match_starts: Vec<Range<usize>>`, the offsets in the hit's text at which a match starts, as ranges of consecutive offsets. The sink finds them with `Matcher::find_iter` over each matching line (`text_matches` and its second searcher are gone). `owned_hits` credits each match to the innermost block whose span holds its first byte, breaking equal spans by depth in the block tree, and a hit goes once to every block that holds one of its matches. The own-text test and the equal-range rule are deleted.
- **The invariant.** Every matched line with a byte in at least one block credits at least one block. Review found two ways to break it, one defect: ownership read match positions from one alternation and credited only a block that held the position strictly, so a line could be credited to nothing and `retrieve_blocks` dropped its blocks without a word. Three rules, in order, now hold it.
  1. A match goes to the innermost block that holds its first byte strictly (`start <= byte < end`).
  2. A match that no block holds strictly, at an offset where a block ends, goes to the innermost block that ends there: the end is inclusive only when no block holds the offset, so `$` after `const needle = 1;` belongs to the declaration and `$` between a method's `}` and its class's `}` belongs to the class. This applies to any match start, not only zero-width ones, because starts are all that is stored; `} x` with `x` right after a block's `}` credits that block, as the old rule did.
  3. A hit that no match credited (its matches begin between blocks, or began past the line cut) goes to the innermost blocks at each byte of its line, which is the old "a match is never lost" rule. A line no block touches has no block to return: a match in an import or a top-level statement is outside every declaration.
- **Per term.** `compile` joins the terms with `|`, and one alternation takes the leftmost match and continues after it, so `class.*` over a line holding `m` never reports `m` and the method starting there got no hit. The sink now runs each term on its own over a matched line and merges the starts. The searcher still uses the alternation to find which lines match.
- **Per match, not per hit.** ADR 0005 said a hit belongs to the block containing its start byte. A line with matches in two sibling blocks (`const a = 1; const needle = 2;` searched for `const`) must keep both, as the line rule did, so ownership is decided for each match. The ADR text is corrected.
- **Starts, not extents.** Ownership reads only where a match begins, so the ranges store starts and merge consecutive ones. A pattern that matches every byte of a line (`.`, `\w`) is one range, not one per byte; an ADR draft stored the extent of each match, 16 bytes each, up to 16 times the line's bytes. A range of several offsets is credited to the innermost block at each of them, which equals one range per offset. The worst case left is a start at every other offset, at most half the line's length in ranges.
- **Lossy offsets.** The searcher reads raw bytes and the analyzer reads the lossy-decoded text. Each hit's starts are mapped to the lossy text of its own line (`lossy_offset`, one pass over the line's `Utf8Chunks`, skipped when the line is valid), and the pipeline adds the line's start in the analyzed text (`hit_line_starts`), so no offset depends on the file's raw bytes. Searching decoded text instead was not tried. A UTF-8 BOM stays in the first line's text, so offsets agree.
- **Line cap.** A match that starts past the 4096th byte of a line is not recorded, but rule 3 gives the hit to the blocks on the kept part of the line, as before.
- **Siblings checked.** Where else a block or a hit can vanish: a required term that matches only past the cut drops the file (the cut-line warning says so, §35); the file ceiling, oversize and binary files are counted or named; a block with no hit is not a candidate by design; test blocks are left out unless asked for. One was silent and now is not: a hit on a line the file no longer has (it shrank after the search) is counted in a warning naming the file.
- **Tests.** `owned_hits` is checked against a plain walk over every block and byte, with random forests including equal spans, and against `regex`-found starts of random patterns (`^`, `$`, `\b`, `a*`, `(?:)`, `a.*b`, alternations and overlapping terms) over random text, where each block must get exactly the lines the rules name and every matched line with a byte in a block must be credited. Exact-value tests cover both review findings (`regex:$` on a declaration; `regex:class.* m` over a multi-line method), `^`, `\b`, a nested class and method, and a test module, in TypeScript and Rust. Exclusions drop a whole file before ownership is read, so they are tested there, not in the property.
- **Output.** Same columns and order. On the pinned repositories a handful of queries differ in `totalCount` (1 to 3 lower) and in the later digits of `finalScore`, because document frequencies count fewer blocks; the rows shown are identical. The harness is unchanged.
- **Deleted.** The reference reimplementation of the old rule in `pipeline/proptests.rs` and its regression seeds.
- **Open.** Memory of the starts: `regex:\b` over 80 MB of source peaked at 2.1 GB against 1.7 GB for main, `regex:.` at 1.7 GB against 1.7 GB, and `regex:.` ran 1.6 times as long because each of up to 4096 bytes of a line is looked up. Freeing a file's hits as soon as its blocks are found was tried and raised the peak, so it was not kept. Step 3 (snippets, name boost, dedup from spans) is not started.

- **Open.** The sets are small, so one miss moves a rate by 4 points; read them as a regression guard, not an estimate. The one held-out miss is trpc `create websocket client` (answer file at rank 7).

## 35. Reads, hit lines and run time have stated bounds (2026-11-11)

Follows [ADR 0004](../adr/0004-search-stays-stateless-and-every-stage-has-a-stated-bound.md) rules 2 to 4 (PR 88).

- **Decision.** Text search reads at most 4 MiB of a file (`MAX_FILE_BYTES`), checked on the open handle. A larger file is skipped unread and reported as one grouped line. A hit line is kept to 4096 bytes (`MAX_LINE_BYTES`) and the cut lines are counted in a warning. `--timeout SECONDS` defaults to 30, accepts fractions, and 0 disables it. It is checked between files in text search and between batches in analysis. Each stage always finishes its first batch, so a tiny timeout still returns something. An expired run prints `partial result: ... expired after searching|analyzing N of M files` and exits 0. `tests/scaling.rs` takes the fastest of 5 runs at 2,500 and 10,000 inputs for rank and dedup, text search and a whole search, and asserts the time ratio stays under 10 (a quadratic step gives 16). It never asserts absolute times.
- **Why.** The limit equals the 4 MiB parse cap, so a larger file could only come back as too large to parse after being read whole. On the PR's measurements a directory of forty 5 MB files peaked at 479 MB and one 300 MB line at 752 MB; both are now about 5 MB.
- **Partial results.** They are the only output that differs between runs, because which files are reached depends on speed. A `-term` exclusion applies only to the files reached. Without a timeout, output is deterministic.
- **Cost of the line cap.** A term that matches only past byte 4096 of a line is not seen by required-term and keyword checks, and since §42 the hit has no match start, though its line still goes to the blocks on it. The warning says so.

## 36. Parse on a fixed stack behind a nesting scan (2026-11-11)

Replaces §23's per-byte stack and its size caps (PR 83).

- **Decision.** Every parse runs on one 256 MiB stack (`PARSE_STACK_BYTES`). A linear scan (`analysis/nesting.rs`) estimates the recursion a file can cause and rejects it before any parser sees it. The cap is 16,384 levels for TypeScript and 256 for Rust. A rejected file is degraded as too deep and named in the diagnostic with its depth and cap. The post-parse tree-depth check and its leaked trees are gone, because no accepted tree is deeper than the drop thread holds. The size cap is 4 MiB (35).
- **Why.** §23's stack grew with the input, so whether a file was analyzed depended on its length and the host's memory. A fixed stack makes cost and outcome a function of the file alone. §23 deleted the scan because it rejected valid files; the scan now errs only upward and is tested against the real parsers.
- **A false rejection, found and fixed.** The first cap (4,096 levels on a 64 MiB stack) rejected a component with 3,000 sibling JSX elements: its true depth is about 3, but closers do not lower the estimate, so it cost about 45,000 units. The cap and the stack grew by 4x together to keep the margin (the worst nesting at the cap needed 96 MiB and overflowed 64 MiB, so 256 MiB is at least 2.6x). End-to-end tests cover 3,000 JSX siblings, a 12,000-term concatenation and a 20,000-row array.
- **Three soundness bugs found by review, fixed.** `for await (` lost its loop head to `await`. A `;` in JSX text reset what the open elements had charged. Each ambiguous `/` rescanned its whole line. Each has a test that parses the input in a child process on a small stack to show the hazard is real.
- **A differential fuzzer.** `soundness_tests.rs` generates nesting-heavy token soups, scans them under a cap scaled to an 8 MiB stack, and parses every accepted input in a child process. An abort is a counterexample. It found more under-estimates, all fixed with regression tests: a template `}` inside a possible regex flipped backtick parity; Rust 2024 `#"` is a prefix, not a string; unterminated strings, templates, comments and raw strings hid the rest of the source; and the Rust cap let trees deeper than the drop thread holds (now 256 levels). On the final code the PR run found no counterexample.
- **Evidence, not proof.** The fuzzer samples inputs; it does not prove the scan never under-estimates. `MONOKL_FUZZ_SECONDS` sets the run length. The estimate stays a deliberate over-estimate wherever the scan cannot tell syntax apart.
- **Threads are reused within a search.** A thread per parse cost 3.5 s of CPU against 35 ms of parsing over 20,000 files on 18 cores, mostly mapping and unmapping 256 MiB stacks. A search now starts its analysis threads once with that stack (`with_parse_threads`), no more than it has files, and none when nothing matched; a parse on one of them runs in place. A parse anywhere else still gets its own thread. The stack, the nesting scan and the 4 MiB cap are unchanged.
- **Open.** A valid file over the cap loses its results and the user sees it by name.

## 37. Deletions of code nothing reads (2026-11-11)

PRs 84 to 87. Each removed code whose only reader was a test or nothing.

- **Decision.** The query module is crate-private, and tests that scanned source text, probed for absent derives or re-checked exhaustiveness are deleted (PR 84). `coverage_boost` is gone (PR 85): every printed block holds a matching line, so it was a constant 1.0, and `finalScore` is 1.0 lower with the order unchanged. The score breakdown fields and `SearchResponse` totals that only tests read are gone, and `SymbolKind` derives `Ord` instead of mirroring it by hand. `--max-bytes`, `Budget.max_bytes`, the `miette` feature and dependency, and `ToonProjection<N>` are gone (PR 86); `render_search` and `search_row_texts` replace the projection, and `apply_budget` takes the printed row texts. Unread analyzer output is gone (PR 87): symbols, dependencies, exports, JSX, `LangData`, the `Digest` and its `blake3` dependency, `AnalysisProfile`, `AnalyzerCapabilities`, `language_for`, `matched_keywords`, `RankedBlock.parent_context` and `ParentContext.line`. `LanguageAnalyzer` is now `languages`, `supports` and `analyze(path, text)`.
- **Why.** Search reads only `blocks`, `test_blocks`, `had_parse_errors` and `degradation`. `--max-tokens` is `ceil(bytes / 3)`, so the 2 MiB byte cap bound only above about 700,000 tokens. CLI errors render through michi's `DomainError`, so the `miette` derives had no use. Unique crates in the workspace tree went from 252 to 232. PR 87 removed 2,440 lines and added 308, and the release binary went from 3,762,592 to 3,696,240 bytes. Output was byte-identical on 101 queries (87) and on 93 comparisons (86; only `search --help` differs).
- **Consequences.** `--max-bytes` is now a usage error (exit 2). A command that needs a removed field restores it with its analyzer output and a reader. [ADR 0002](../adr/0002-digest-lives-in-monokl-until-wisp-contracts.md) stands for whoever re-adds `Digest`. `LanguageId` keeps `TypeScript` and `Rust`.
- **Open.** The `Language`/`LanguageId` unification. The architecture docs still describe `miette` and `max_bytes`.

## 38. Process lessons (2026-11-11)

- **Decision.** Compile and test the combined state before merging a PR that other PRs touch, and run the soundness tests under plain `cargo test` as well as `nextest`.
- **Why.** Two merges broke `main` because each PR passed alone. The object-member score tests (PR 70) were written before the name bonus (§32) and failed once both were in. The scaling test (PR 88) constructed a field that a deletion (PR 85) removed; PR 90 fixed it. CI on a branch checks that branch against the `main` it started from, not against what merges beside it.
- **A real race hid behind one runner.** The soundness tests passed under `nextest` (one process per test) but shared one batch file under `cargo test`, where concurrent child launches overwrote each other's file and removed each other's directory. Each batch now has its own directory (PR 89).

## 39. A block carries the name its analyzer read from the syntax tree (2026-11-12)

- **Decision.** `CodeBlock` gains `name: Option<String>`, filled by both analyzers for every block that declares an identifier, and `name_match_boost` tokenizes it. §32's text-derived name (the signature or first non-comment line, cut at `(`, `<`, `{`, `=` or `:`, with a `pub(crate)` special case for Rust) is deleted. This is the `name` slice of [ADR 0005](../adr/0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md); spans and parent indices stay open.
- **What the name is.** A function, class, interface, type alias, enum, namespace, method, property or constant has its identifier. An `impl` has its target, or `Trait for Target`, the same string its members use as `parent.name`. A member key that is a string literal or a private identifier has its text; a computed key has none. A declaration of several variables takes the first plain identifier. A re-export, an anonymous default export, a destructuring declaration, a macro call and an `extern` block have `None` and get no name boost.
- **Why.** The head of a line is not a name: it held modifiers (`get`, `static`, `default`) and the type of a variable as words, and needed a `pub(crate)` rule because `(` ends the head. The tree has the name.
- **Output.** No column is added. Scores differ only where the old head held a word the name does not (a modifier, or the type of a variable) and for `export default Button;`, which now has no name because it declares none. The harness is unchanged: identifier 58/59, questions 17/18, members 15/16, Rust fd 22/24, held-out 23/24 and 12/12.
- **Not done.** A typed `ParsedTerm` for ranking. `rank_blocks` and `name_match_boost` take BM25 tokens, which are lowercased fragments of the user's words and not query terms, and `ParsedTerm` already types the one place a query term is read (`QueryPlan`). A wrapper around `&str` tokens would add a type with no new check.

## 40. Blocks carry a byte span and a parent index (2026-11-14)

- **Decision.** `CodeBlock` gains `span: Range<usize>` and `parent_index: Option<usize>`, set by both analyzers from the span and the enclosing block they already hold when they build a block. Nothing reads them. This is step 1 of [ADR 0005](../adr/0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md); `name` landed in §39 and `kind` was already typed (`node_kind`), so steps 2 (match ranges in the sink, innermost-containing `owned_hits`) and 3 (snippets, name boost and dedup from spans) remain.
- **Index space.** `parent_index` counts `FileAnalysis::blocks` followed by `FileAnalysis::test_blocks`. The Rust analyzer splits test code into its own list, and a `#[test]` method of a non-test `impl` has its parent in the other list, so one list per kind cannot hold the link. The analyzer records blocks in one list and renumbers when it splits.
- **Offsets are the analyzer's.** `span` counts bytes of the lossy-decoded source the analyzer received, not of the file. Mapping the searcher's raw offsets onto it is step 2's work, as ADR 0005 states.
- **Output.** None. No reader, no wire change, harness unchanged.

## 41. The held-out set widens to Rust and two more TypeScript and JavaScript styles (2026-11-14)

- **Decision.** Four repositories join the held-out rows, none sampled for identifiers and none tuned on: tokio v1.54.1 (macro-heavy), axum v0.8.9 (trait and impl heavy), react-hook-form v7.92.0 (hooks library) and commander v15.1.0 (class-based JavaScript CLI). Questions were written from READMEs and source with `rg` before monokl ran on them. A repository marked `report-only` in `rg-compare.repos` is scored and printed but never gates. Gated held-out Rust rows pool on a `held-out rust` line (`--min-heldout-rust-recall`, 0.9).
- **First scores.** tokio 16 of 16, axum 18 of 20, commander 19 of 19 (now gated), react-hook-form 12 of 14 (report-only). The older held-out lines are unchanged in rows, now pooled with commander.
- **Misses, left as written.** axum `listener extension` (ListenerExt, answer file at rank 9; `extension.rs` and extractor files outrank it on the word `extension`), axum `extractor from request parts` (FromRequestParts, rank 4; `axum-macros/src/lib.rs` and `with_rejection.rs` outrank the trait file), react-hook-form `watch form values subscribe` (useWatch, rank 4; `types/form.ts`, `useFormContext.tsx` and an `app/` page outrank it) and `create form control` (createFormControl, rank 12; `useFormControlContext.ts`, `useForm.ts` and `examples/` files outrank it).

## 42. A match is credited to the block it starts in (2026-11-14)

Step 2 of [ADR 0005](../adr/0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md). Replaces the line-text rule of §31.

- **Decision.** `LineHit` gains `match_starts: Vec<Range<usize>>`, the offsets in the hit's text at which a match starts, as ranges of consecutive offsets. The sink finds them with `Matcher::find_iter` over each matching line (`text_matches` and its second searcher are gone). `owned_hits` credits each match to the innermost block whose span holds its first byte, breaking equal spans by depth in the block tree, and a hit goes once to every block that holds one of its matches. The own-text test and the equal-range rule are deleted.
- **The invariant.** Every matched line with a byte in at least one block credits at least one block. Review found two ways to break it, one defect: ownership read match positions from one alternation and credited only a block that held the position strictly, so a line could be credited to nothing and `retrieve_blocks` dropped its blocks without a word. Three rules, in order, now hold it.
  1. A match goes to the innermost block that holds its first byte strictly (`start <= byte < end`).
  2. A match that no block holds strictly, at an offset where a block ends, goes to the innermost block that ends there: the end is inclusive only when no block holds the offset, so `$` after `const needle = 1;` belongs to the declaration and `$` between a method's `}` and its class's `}` belongs to the class. This applies to any match start, not only zero-width ones, because starts are all that is stored; `} x` with `x` right after a block's `}` credits that block, as the old rule did.
  3. A hit that no match credited (its matches begin between blocks, or began past the line cut) goes to the innermost blocks at each byte of its line, which is the old "a match is never lost" rule. A line no block touches has no block to return: a match in an import or a top-level statement is outside every declaration.
- **Per term.** `compile` joins the terms with `|`, and one alternation takes the leftmost match and continues after it, so `class.*` over a line holding `m` never reports `m` and the method starting there got no hit. The sink now runs each term on its own over a matched line and merges the starts. The searcher still uses the alternation to find which lines match.
- **Per match, not per hit.** ADR 0005 said a hit belongs to the block containing its start byte. A line with matches in two sibling blocks (`const a = 1; const needle = 2;` searched for `const`) must keep both, as the line rule did, so ownership is decided for each match. The ADR text is corrected.
- **Starts, not extents.** Ownership reads only where a match begins, so the ranges store starts and merge consecutive ones. A pattern that matches every byte of a line (`.`, `\w`) is one range, not one per byte; an ADR draft stored the extent of each match, 16 bytes each, up to 16 times the line's bytes. A range of several offsets is credited to the innermost block at each of them, which equals one range per offset. The worst case left is a start at every other offset, at most half the line's length in ranges.
- **Lossy offsets.** The searcher reads raw bytes and the analyzer reads the lossy-decoded text. Each hit's starts are mapped to the lossy text of its own line (`lossy_offset`, one pass over the line's `Utf8Chunks`, skipped when the line is valid), and the pipeline adds the line's start in the analyzed text (`hit_line_starts`), so no offset depends on the file's raw bytes. Searching decoded text instead was not tried. A UTF-8 BOM stays in the first line's text, so offsets agree.
- **Line cap.** A match that starts past the 4096th byte of a line is not recorded, but rule 3 gives the hit to the blocks on the kept part of the line, as before.
- **Siblings checked.** Where else a block or a hit can vanish: a required term that matches only past the cut drops the file (the cut-line warning says so, §35); the file ceiling, oversize and binary files are counted or named; a block with no hit is not a candidate by design; test blocks are left out unless asked for. One was silent and now is not: a hit on a line the file no longer has (it shrank after the search) is counted in a warning naming the file.
- **Tests.** `owned_hits` is checked against a plain walk over every block and byte, with random forests including equal spans, and against `regex`-found starts of random patterns (`^`, `$`, `\b`, `a*`, `(?:)`, `a.*b`, alternations and overlapping terms) over random text, where each block must get exactly the lines the rules name and every matched line with a byte in a block must be credited. Exact-value tests cover both review findings (`regex:$` on a declaration; `regex:class.* m` over a multi-line method), `^`, `\b`, a nested class and method, and a test module, in TypeScript and Rust. Exclusions drop a whole file before ownership is read, so they are tested there, not in the property.
- **Output.** Same columns and order. On the pinned repositories a handful of queries differ in `totalCount` (1 to 3 lower) and in the later digits of `finalScore`, because document frequencies count fewer blocks; the rows shown are identical. The harness is unchanged.
- **Deleted.** The reference reimplementation of the old rule in `pipeline/proptests.rs` and its regression seeds.
- **Open.** Memory of the starts: `regex:\b` over 80 MB of source peaked at 2.1 GB against 1.7 GB for main, `regex:.` at 1.7 GB against 1.7 GB, and `regex:.` ran 1.6 times as long because each of up to 4096 bytes of a line is looked up. Freeing a file's hits as soon as its blocks are found was tried and raised the peak, so it was not kept. Step 3 (snippets, name boost, dedup from spans) is not started.

content.content:
# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install the cargo tools the recipes below use
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest cargo-llvm-cov cargo-machete cargo-mutants cargo-deny typos-cli zizmor --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Install the pinned toolchain and the moon-managed git hooks
setup:
    proto install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

# Build the workspace. One `cargo --workspace` invocation, not `moon run :build`: per-crate cargo processes all
# contend for the same target/ lock and serialize.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --locked

build-release:
    cargo build --workspace --release --locked

# Run tests with nextest, plus doctests, which nextest does not run. The default-features pass catches code that only
# builds because --all-features turned something on.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --locked
    cargo nextest run --workspace --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --all-features --locked

# Line coverage; fails below the threshold, which this default owns
coverage threshold="90":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{ threshold }}"

# Coverage report, opened in the browser
coverage-html:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --html --open

# Format check, clippy with and without default features, and typos, the same as CI's lint job
lint: typos
    cargo fmt --all --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-default-features --locked -- -D warnings

# Clippy on the crates moon reports as affected, in one cargo invocation
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then exit 0; fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings

fmt:
    cargo fmt --all

# Documentation build, with warnings (including broken intra-doc links) as errors
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --all-features --locked
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --locked

# Licenses, advisories, bans and sources
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Unused dependencies
machete:
    cargo machete

typos:
    typos

# Callisto config, package discovery and pending changesets; the same gate as CI's Changesets job
changesets:
    callisto status --check --strict
    callisto release --dry-run --format text

# Record a pending change for the next release, e.g. `just changeset minor "Add the search command"`
changeset bump summary:
    callisto add --package cargo/monokl:{{ bump }} --summary "{{ summary }}"

# Workflow audit for permission, credential and supply-chain issues
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Fails when a duplicated fact disagrees with its owner, e.g. the Callisto pin in the workflows against .prototools
check-drift:
    scripts/check-drift.sh

# Checks a published release is complete and usable, e.g. `just verify-release 0.4.0`. Needs network and gh.
verify-release version:
    scripts/verify-release.sh {{ version }}

# Score search targeting and output size against ripgrep on pinned public repos. Needs network and `rg`; on demand, not part of `just ci`.
rg-compare *args:
    cargo build --release -q
    python3 -I scripts/rg-compare.py {{ args }}

# Time and peak memory of `monokl search` against ripgrep on pinned repos and a stress set. Warm cache; needs network and `rg`; on demand.
bench *args:
    cargo build --release -q
    python3 -I scripts/bench.py {{ args }}

# Block span and parent invariants over the harness repositories in target/rg-compare (`just rg-compare` fills it) or the directories in MONOKL_SPAN_CORPUS; skips with a message when neither exists. On demand.
span-invariants:
    cargo test -p monokl --test span_invariants --release -- --ignored --nocapture

# Mutation testing. Slow, so on demand only, not part of `just ci`.
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# Public API SemVer check against the last published version. Not in `just ci` until a first release exists.
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

clean:
    moon clean 2>/dev/null || true

"""Runs the old and the new monokl over the same queries on the pinned repositories and reports each differing output."""
import difflib
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/.claude/worktrees/agent-a3f673a53d0186c7c")
OLD = ROOT / "target/old-build/release/monokl"
NEW = ROOT / "target/release/monokl"
CACHE = ROOT / "target/rg-compare"

questions = []
for line in (ROOT / "scripts/rg-compare.questions").read_text().splitlines():
    if not line.strip() or line.startswith("#"):
        continue
    parts = [p.strip() for p in line.split("|")]
    questions.append((parts[0], parts[1]))

extra = ["string", "error", "export", "return", "this", "regex:\\w+ Error", "async function", "regex:^\\s*}"]
repos = sorted(p.name for p in CACHE.iterdir() if p.is_dir())
queries = [(repo, q) for repo, q in questions if repo in repos]
queries += [(repo, q) for repo in repos for q in extra]


def run(binary, repo, query):
    out = subprocess.run([str(binary), "search", query, "."], cwd=CACHE / repo, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return out.returncode, out.stdout, out.stderr


differ = 0
for repo, query in queries:
    old, new = run(OLD, repo, query), run(NEW, repo, query)
    if old != new:
        differ += 1
        print(f"=== {repo}: {query!r}  (exit {old[0]} -> {new[0]})")
        diff = difflib.unified_diff(old[1].splitlines(), new[1].splitlines(), "old", "new", lineterm="", n=0)
        for i, line in enumerate(diff):
            if i > 12:
                print("   ...")
                break
            print("   " + line[:220])
        if old[2] != new[2]:
            print("   stderr differs:", old[2][:200], "|", new[2][:200])

```

`search_patterns()` deliberately omits `excluded` — exclusion terms never drive text search; they
apply as a post-match filter in the pipeline's boolean evaluation stage.

**Exclusion-only queries (finding #21, resolved by 05 §21).** A query with no positive term (`-foo -bar`, or an empty
query) returns no results and one `Skipped` diagnostic saying the query has no positive terms, so it is not mistaken for "matched nothing."

## Ranking (`rank/`)

```rust
pub fn rank_blocks(blocks: Vec<(CodeBlock, Vec<String>)>, query_terms: &[&str], df: &HashMap<...>)
    -> Vec<RankedBlock>
```

Per block: `bm25 = bm25::score(...)`,
`ntype = boost::node_type_boost(block.node_kind)`, `name = boost::name_match_boost(&block, query_terms)`
(1 + 2 * share of query terms in the block's declared name, `CodeBlock.name`, so 1.0 to 3.0; 1.0 for a block with no name),
**`final_score = round6(bm25 * name * ntype)`**.
Sorted by `final_score` descending, then file, `line_start`, `line_end`, `node_kind` and `code`; 1-based `rank` is
assigned after the sort.

BM25 (`rank/bm25.rs`): `K1 = 1.5`, `B = 0.5`, standard Okapi formula, `round6` to 6dp for
cross-platform f64 stability (`DP = 1_000_000.0`) — keep this rounding.

`node_type_boost` (`rank/boost.rs`): Function 1.5; Class/Method/Constructor 1.4; Interface/Struct
1.3; TypeAlias/Enum 1.2; Variable/Impl 1.1; Property/Field/Macro 1.0; Module 0.9; Other 0.7.

## Determinism and bounds

Resolved findings, kept so they are not reopened:

1. **#7 — a bad `regex:` term fails the whole search.** Every term, excluded ones too, compiles before any file is
   read (05 §18).
2. **#9 — total-order tie-break.** The six sort keys above leave no ties, so the order never depends on input order.
3. **#10 — the file walk is sorted by file name**, so the set of files reached under the file ceiling is reproducible.
4. **#11 — resource bounds.** The text search examines at most 100,000 files and keeps counting past it, reads at most
   4 MiB per file and keeps 4096 bytes per line; `--max-results` and `--max-tokens` cut the output; `--timeout` stops
   the work. See [ADR 0004](../adr/0004-search-stays-stateless-and-every-stage-has-a-stated-bound.md).

Open:

- **#16 — no cap on one term's or the query's length.** `LIMIT = 64` bounds term *count* only. Decide whether a length
  cap is needed, and which error reports it (a sibling to `TooManyTerms`, not a repurposing of it).

# Core Types — Semantic Model

Source: `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md` §4 ("types.rs — all public types verbatim"). `crates/monokl/src/types.rs`
implements the part of it that search reads. This file states what `types.rs` contains.

None of these types derives `Serialize` or `Deserialize`: wire shapes belong to the output layer. A type with no
caller is not defined (see the decision-log entry "Removed public types nothing builds or consumes" in
`05-research-and-decisions.md`), so the spec's `SearchOptions`, `SearchLimits`, `SymbolsResult`, `DependentsResult`,
`TsconfigMode`, `WorkspaceOptions` and `ExtractRequest` are not in `types.rs` until a command uses them.

## CodeBlock / RankedBlock / ParentContext

```rust
pub struct CodeBlock {
    pub file: Utf8PathBuf,
    pub line_start: usize,
    pub line_end: usize,
    pub node_kind: SymbolKind,
    pub span: Range<usize>,
    pub parent_index: Option<usize>,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub code: String,
    pub symbol_signature: Option<String>,
    pub matched_lines: Vec<usize>,
    pub parent: Option<ParentContext>,
}

pub struct RankedBlock {
    pub block: CodeBlock,
    pub final_score: f64,
    pub rank: usize,
}

pub struct ParentContext { pub kind: SymbolKind, pub name: String }
```

`RankedBlock` nests its `CodeBlock`; the output layer picks the columns it prints.
`CodeBlock.name` is the identifier the block declares, read from the syntax tree by the analyzer (`Trait for Target` for a trait `impl`); it is `None` for a re-export, an anonymous default export, a destructuring declaration, a macro call and an `extern` block. Ranking reads it for the name boost, and nothing prints it.
`CodeBlock.span` is the byte range of the analyzed source the block covers, so `source[span] == code`. The analyzer receives the file's lossy UTF-8 decoding, so offsets match the file's own bytes only until the first invalid sequence. `CodeBlock.parent_index` is the position of the enclosing block in `FileAnalysis::blocks` followed by `FileAnalysis::test_blocks`; it is `Some` exactly when `parent` is, and the parent is earlier in that order and its span contains the block's. A Rust test member of a non-test `impl` therefore points from `test_blocks` into `blocks`. Nothing reads either field yet ([ADR 0005](../adr/0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md), step 1).
`CodeBlock.parent` is the enclosing class or object literal of a member block and `None` for a top-level block; the analyzer sets it, and the agent output prints it as the `parent` column (`<kind> <name>`).
`final_score` is the only score `RankedBlock` carries; see `query-and-ranking.md` for the ranking algorithm itself, not covered here.

## `Language`

One enum names the languages monokl searches, and `analysis/lang.rs` holds every file fact about them:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "cli", derive(clap::ValueEnum))]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum Language { TypeScript, JavaScript, Rust }
```

- `Language::of(path)` is the language of a file, `None` for an unsearched extension and for `.d.ts`, `.d.mts` and `.d.cts`.
- `Language::rules()` has the extensions, the excluded suffixes and the test-file names; `is_test_path` adds the test directories.
- The CLI's `--language` flag, the `--language` filter in the pipeline, `LanguageAnalyzer::supports` and `languages`, text search's test-file skip and the rg-compare and bench scripts (through the hidden `monokl language-rules`) all read these rules. Add an extension in `lang.rs` only.
- `LanguageAnalyzer::languages` is a slice because one analyzer can own several languages: `TsAnalyzer` owns `TypeScript` and `JavaScript`.
- A variant exists when a language has an analyzer. `Python` was removed because nothing handled it: `--language python` is a usage error (exit 2) that lists the valid values.

content.content:
## Pull requests

- CI's aggregate `CI` check must pass: lint, tests on Linux and macOS, MSRV, line coverage, and audit. The same checks run on the merge queue's combined commit and again on every push to main; a red main opens or updates a `ci-red` issue.
- Keep a PR to one topic.
- A change users can see needs a changeset. Internal changes (tests, CI, docs, refactors) do not.

## Writing a changeset

Each changeset becomes one bullet in the changelog. Each version lists its bullets under `Major Changes`, `Minor Changes` and `Patch Changes` headings, below the release date and a compare link. The release PR titles each change by its first line and collapses the rest.

- **One topic per file** in `.changeset/`, with `monokl: minor` for a new capability or `monokl: patch` for a fix.
- **Entries appear in filename order within their bump heading.** Prefix a filename with `0-` (then `1-`) to make an entry lead its heading.
- **Put identifiers, flags and syntax in backticks.**
- `just changesets` validates them. The rendered text only shows in the release PR, so read it there before merging.

Changesets become the project's changelog, so write them for the people who use it, not for the implementer.

- Open with a bold lead-in naming the change as the user sees it, then one line on its value: what they can now do or what changed for them.
- When there is more to say, add short bullets in this order: why it matters, how to adopt it (commands, configuration, migration), and limits they will hit. Use sub-bullets for detail.
- Group a longer entry under bold labels such as **Upgrading** or **Scripting**. Do not use `#` headings; the changelog supplies those.
- Put a breaking change in its own paragraph starting `**Breaking:**` (old behavior, new behavior, what to do), and a step users must take in one starting `**Action:**`. Never inside a bullet: the release PR lists them under "Read before merging" only as paragraphs. A removed or renamed flag, a removed or non-public library item, a changed output shape or value and a library signature change are breaking.
- One idea per bullet. Leave out internals unless the user must know them.

## Filing an issue

Say what you expected, what happened, and, if it's a spec-vs-reality mismatch, which file in `docs/spec/` you were reading.
---
monokl: minor
---

Blocks carry the byte span they cover and the position of the block that encloses them, so later stages can tell blocks apart by where they are and not by their text.

- **Span.** `CodeBlock::span` is the byte range of the analyzed source the block covers, so `source[span] == code`. Offsets count bytes of the text the analyzer received, which is the lossy UTF-8 decoding of a file with invalid bytes.
- **Parent.** `CodeBlock::parent_index` is the position of the enclosing block in `FileAnalysis::blocks` followed by `FileAnalysis::test_blocks`. It is set exactly when `parent` is, for the members of a class, object literal, `impl`, trait or inline module.
- **No change to results.** Nothing reads either field yet: `monokl search` output and the harness scores are unchanged.

**Breaking:** `CodeBlock` has two new public fields. Code that builds one must set `span` and `parent_index`.
---
monokl: minor
---

**A match is credited to the block it sits in.** `monokl search` decides which block holds a matching line by where in the line each match starts, not by comparing the text of the line, so a match is never given to a block that only shares its line, and a line a block covers is never lost.

- **Why it matters.** A class or object keeps a match that is its own even when a method on the same line matches another term, and blocks that share a line (`} b() {`, `}, // note`, `const a = 1; const needle = 2;`) are told apart by the byte where the match begins. A test function and the module that holds it are never both credited.
- **Terms are searched one by one.** `regex:class.* m` finds the method `m` that starts on the line `class.*` matches; the terms used to be joined, and the first match hid the second.
- **End of a declaration.** `regex:$` and other matches at the end of a declaration belong to it.
- **Output.** Same columns and the same order. On the pinned repositories the shown rows are identical, `totalCount` is 1 to 3 lower in a few queries, and `finalScore` moves in its later digits where fewer blocks change the document frequencies. Harness scores are unchanged.
- **A shrunken file.** Matching lines past the end of a file that changed after it was searched are counted in a warning.

**Breaking:** `LineHit` has a new public field, `match_starts`, the offsets in the hit's text at which a match starts. Code that builds a `LineHit` must set it, and `text_search` fills it.

**Two blocks that share a line are no longer taken for one.** `monokl search` removes a block that repeats a better one by the bytes the two share, not the lines, and decides what a snippet leaves out by where the signature ends, not by comparing text.

- **Why it matters.** `const first = 1; const second = 2;` and `fn a() {} fn b() {}` each used to give one row, because both blocks claimed line 1 and the second counted as a copy of the first. Each block that holds a match now gets its row. A block inside another, or equal to it, is still dropped as before.
- **Snippets.** A matching line is left out when the signature column already shows all of it, wherever that line is in the block: the lines of a multi-line signature, and the signature line of a Rust item below its attributes or doc comments, no longer repeat the signature in the snippet. A line that says more than the signature stays: a decorator, the start of an arrow function's expression body, or a body on the same line.
- **Output.** Same columns and the same order. A search can return more rows where blocks shared a line, and fewer snippet lines where the signature spans several.

**Breaking:** `CodeBlock` has a new public field, `signature_span`, the bytes of the declaration's head that `symbol_signature` is the one-line form of. Code that builds a `CodeBlock` must set it, with `None` for a block that has no signature.

**Breaking:** `dedup_blocks` compares `CodeBlock::span`, not `line_start` and `line_end`. A caller that built blocks with an empty span (`0..0`) now has every one of them kept; set each block's real span.

"""Runs two monokl binaries over the same queries on the pinned repositories and reports each differing output.

usage: compare_outputs.py OLD_BINARY NEW_BINARY
"""
import difflib
import subprocess
import sys
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/.claude/worktrees/agent-aea747ffca5852cb9")
OLD, NEW = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])
CACHE = ROOT / "target/rg-compare"

rows = []
for line in (ROOT / "scripts/rg-compare.questions").read_text().splitlines():
    if not line.strip() or line.startswith("#"):
        continue
    parts = [p.strip() for p in line.split("|")]
    rows.append((parts[0], parts[1], parts[3] if len(parts) > 3 else ""))

extra = ["string", "error", "export", "return", "this", "regex:\\w+ Error", "async function", "regex:^\\s*}", "regex:{}",
         "regex:\\)\\s*{", "regex:;\\s*\\w"]
repos = sorted(p.name for p in CACHE.iterdir() if p.is_dir())
queries = []
for repo, question, symbol in rows:
    if repo in repos:
        queries.append((repo, question))
        if symbol and symbol != "-":
            queries.append((repo, symbol))
queries += [(repo, q) for repo in repos for q in extra]
queries = list(dict.fromkeys(queries))


def run(binary, repo, query):
    out = subprocess.run([str(binary), "search", query, "."], cwd=CACHE / repo, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return out.returncode, out.stdout, out.stderr


def both(item):
    repo, query = item
    return item, run(OLD, repo, query), run(NEW, repo, query)


differ = 0
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=3) as pool:
    for (repo, query), old, new in pool.map(both, queries):
        if old != new:
            differ += 1
            print(f"=== {repo}: {query!r}  (exit {old[0]} -> {new[0]})")
            diff = difflib.unified_diff(old[1].splitlines(), new[1].splitlines(), "old", "new", lineterm="", n=0)
            for i, line in enumerate(diff):
                if i > 16:
                    print("   ...")
                    break
                print("   " + line[:260])
            if old[2] != new[2]:
                print("   stderr differs:", old[2][:200], "|", new[2][:200])
print(f"{differ} of {len(queries)} queries differ")

Each does less work on fewer candidates than the one before. ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'lineColor': '#64748b', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#f8fafc', 'fontFamily': 'ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif'}}}%% flowchart TB S1["1 · Parse the query
+required / -excluded / bare-optional / #quot;phrase#quot; / regex:pattern"] S2["2 · Canonicalize the search root"] S3["3 · Text search
grep-searcher, the crate ripgrep is built on, over the sorted file walk; stops at the timeout"] S4["4 · Boolean evaluation
drop files missing a required term or containing an excluded one"] S5["5 · Block retrieval
analyze survivors, keep only blocks overlapping a matched line"] S6["6 · BM25 rank — K1=1.5, B=0.5
x node-type boost (functions over modules)
x name-match boost (query words in the declared name)"] S7["7 · Dedup
drop blocks overlapping >50% with a higher-ranked block in the same file"] S8["8 · Budget
cut to --max-results and --max-tokens, with a help line saying how many were cut"] S1 --> S2 --> S3 --> S4 --> S5 --> S6 --> S7 --> S8 style S1 fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a style S2 fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a style S3 fill:#e0e7ff,stroke:#4338ca,color:#312e81 style S4 fill:#e0e7ff,stroke:#4338ca,color:#312e81 style S5 fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#4c1d95 style S6 fill:#d1fae5,stroke:#059669,color:#064e3b style S7 fill:#d1fae5,stroke:#059669,color:#064e3b style S8 fill:#fed7aa,stroke:#ea580c,color:#7c2d12 ``` Stages 1 to 7 are core and cap nothing. Stage 8 and the output format live in the agent layer ([ADR 0003](docs/adr/0003-single-crate-with-core-and-agent-modules.md)), which prints through [michi](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi). Search holds no state between runs ([ADR 0004](docs/adr/0004-search-stays-stateless-and-every-stage-has-a-stated-bound.md)). Each stage has a stated bound: file size, line length, nesting, file count and time. See [Limits](README.md#limits). ## Planned Nothing below is built. Each is a design in `docs/spec/`. - **Cache.** An in-memory and disk cache of per-file analyses, keyed by content hash. Search is stateless today, and the design is in [cache-architecture.md](docs/architecture/cache-architecture.md). - **Workspace index.** A `WorkspaceEnricher` layer would fold per-file analyses into an import graph and a symbol index without re-parsing. It needs the dependency and symbol output that was deleted because no command read it. - **More commands.** `symbols`, `refs`, `definition` and `dependents`, which the index would serve. - **Library session API.** A `Workspace` opened once, with snapshots and provenance, for embedders. See [`08-library-session-api.md`](docs/spec/08-library-session-api.md). - **Per-operation precision.** A `CapabilityPrecision` level per analyzer operation, once a command needs to gate on it. - **More languages.** Python, Go and Java. The registry takes a new analyzer without changing the pipeline. - **Daemon and session mode.** See [daemon-lifetimes.md](docs/architecture/daemon-lifetimes.md). ## What's explicitly out of scope Full list and rationale in [PRINCIPLES.md](PRINCIPLES.md#non-goals). Briefly: - No persistent search index. - No embedding-based retrieval by default. - No stemming. - No in-memory trigram index. - No tree-sitter for TypeScript or JavaScript. - No full [Salsa](https://github.com/salsa-rs/salsa) incremental framework. An open investigation, not ruled out. ``` Each row is one match: where it is (`file`, `lineStart`, `lineEnd`), what it is (`nodeKind`: function, class, method, interface, type alias and so on), what holds it (`parent`), its signature, the lines in it that matched (`snippet`), and its `rank` and `finalScore`. Output uses [TOON](https://github.com/toon-format/spec), a table format that costs fewer tokens than JSON. A method, a constructor, or a class property holding an arrow function or a function expression gets a row of its own when it spans three lines or more and its class is declared at the top level of the file or exported. So does a method, getter, setter, or a property holding an arrow function or a function expression, of an object literal that is assigned to a top-level `const`, `let` or `var`, or The `snippet` is the lines of the block that matched, each with its line number and cut at 160 characters. It shows up to three, then counts the rest (`...and 2 more matching lines`). A block's first line is left out when the signature already shows all of it, so the snippet is `null` when that line is the only match. A first line that says more than the signature stays in, such as a decorator or ## Writing a query | You write | It means |

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Times `monokl search` against `rg` on pinned repositories and on a synthetic stress set. Not a correctness check.

Per (repo, query class, tool): `--runs` timed runs after `--warmups` untimed ones, reported as p50 and p95 wall ms, the
peak resident set size over the runs (from `/usr/bin/time`, macOS `-l` or Linux `-v`) and the bytes of output.
Everything is warm: the warm-ups and repeated runs leave the files in the OS page cache, and cold-cache runs are not
measured. A run that exits with a status above 1 or dies is a crash and a run over 60 s is a TIMEOUT; either makes the
script exit non-zero. There are no thresholds.

Query classes: identifier (a declared name), words (three declared names), broad (a very common word), regex
(`regex:\\bPREFIX\\w+`), nomatch (a word that occurs nowhere) and path (the broad word restricted to the directory
that declares the identifier). Identifiers are sampled from top-level declarations as rg-compare.py does, so the choice
is deterministic for a pinned checkout.

The stress set is generated into target/bench/stress: a 5 MB single-line JavaScript file, a 50,000-line generated
TypeScript file and 20,000 small files that each contain `needle`. `needle` is searched in each, with rg for comparison.

Repositories are cloned shallow into target/bench on demand.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import signal
import statistics
import importlib.util
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
MANIFEST = ROOT / "scripts" / "bench.repos"
CACHE = ROOT / "target" / "bench"
# rg-compare.py reads monokl's file and test rules from the binary; its file name has a hyphen, so load it by path.
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("rg_compare", ROOT / "scripts" / "rg-compare.py")
RG_COMPARE = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
_spec.loader.exec_module(RG_COMPARE)
TIMEOUT_S = 60
NO_MATCH = "zqxjvkwpnomatchzz"
DARWIN = sys.platform == "darwin"
TIME = ["/usr/bin/time", "-l" if DARWIN else "-v"]

# language -> (top-level declaration regex, broad word). The regex is copied from rg-compare.py; the globs come from
# monokl itself through rg-compare.py's `configure`.
LANGS = {
    "ts": (
        r"^(?:export\s+)?(?:default\s+)?(?:declare\s+)?(?:abstract\s+)?(?:async\s+)?(?:function\*?|class|interface|type|enum|const|let|var)\s+",
        "string",
    ),
    "rust": (
        r"^(?:pub(?:\([a-z:]+\))?\s+)?(?:(?:const|async|unsafe|extern(?:\s+\"[A-Za-z]+\")?)\s+)*(?:fn|struct|enum|trait|type|const|static|mod|macro_rules!)\s+",
        "error",
    ),
}


def run(args, cwd=None, check=True):
    return subprocess.run(args, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=check)

Step 3 of [ADR 0005](docs/adr/0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md), the last. **Base is `feat/span-hit-ownership` (#105), so this must merge after #105.** When #105 merges, retarget to `main`.

## What changes

- `snippet` leaves out a matched line that lies inside the block's new `signature_span` (the bytes of the declaration's head, `export`/`pub` included, through the `{` that opens a block body, past the `}` of an empty body). `signature_shows` and its modifier list are deleted.
- `dedup_blocks` compares `CodeBlock::span` and drops a block sharing more than half of the smaller span's bytes with a kept block in the same file. ADR 0005 states "compares bytes instead of lines" and no other rule, so the half-of-the-smaller test stays, in bytes. Analyzer spans nest or are disjoint, so it means containment or equality. Two blocks that share a line but no byte (`const a = 1; const b = 2;`, `fn a() {} fn b() {}`) are no longer one block.
- Both analyzers fill `signature_span` where they build the signature. `span_invariants` checks it (set exactly when the signature is, inside the block, its text holds the signature).
- The set-based and unindexed reference reimplementations in `dedup/proptests.rs` are replaced by contract properties: input order and consecutive ranks, no survivor repeats an earlier one, every dropped block repeats a survivor, and blocks with no shared byte all survive.
- `name_match_boost` needed nothing: §39 already moved it to `CodeBlock::name`.
- Docs: decision log §43, ADR 0005, `core-types.md`, `query-and-ranking.md`, README, ARCHITECTURE. Changeset: minor, with two `Breaking:` notes (`CodeBlock::signature_span`, `dedup_blocks` reads spans).

## Output differences

Old and new binaries were run over 421 queries on the pinned repositories (every `questions` row, its answer symbol, and 11 generic queries per repository), against #105 and against `main`; both give the same result.

- No query changes its rows, ranks or scores. 184 of 421 print a different snippet and nothing else.
- Each difference is a signature line removed from a snippet, with the next matching lines moving up into the three shown. Kinds: parameters and return type of a multi-line TypeScript signature (zustand, zod, trpc, fastify), and the `fn` line of a Rust item below doc comments or attributes (fd, tokio, axum). A script checked all removed lines: each is inside the row's signature cell. No line was added except one that moved up.
- Byte-based dedup changes no harness query. The old binary gives one row for `const first = 1; const second = 2;` searched for `first second`; the new gives two (`tests/cli.rs`, TypeScript and Rust).
- `a_match_that_spans_the_edge_of_every_block_on_its_line_is_still_found` queried `regex:1; const`, which is two terms, and passed because dedup dropped the second block. It now queries one term, `regex:1;.const`, and a new test pins the two-term case.

## Checks

By exit code, `just lint` (1.99.1), `just test`, `just rg-compare`, `just changesets` and `just bench` all exit 0. CI is pending. Harness: identifier 58/59, questions 17/18, members 15/16, Rust fd 22/24, held-out 32/33 and 22/22, held-out rust 34/36 (unchanged). Bench, old against new binary alternating five rounds, minimum p50: `stress/many` 459.9 to 470.3 ms (+2.3%), `stress/biggen` 48.8 to 49.5 ms, `stress/bigline` 6.7 to 6.6 ms.

## Left of ADR 0005

Nothing planned. `code` is still copied into every block, so nested blocks duplicate text; a block could slice it from the file.
